papers.title: Harmonic analysis and circuit approximation of Sobolev functions on quantum input spaces
papers.abstract: We derive approximation rates for Sobolev functions defined on the complex unit sphere and complex projective space, representing quantum states, and on the special and projective unitary groups, representing quantum unitary operations. By using harmonic analysis on compact groups and compact homogeneous spaces, we characterize the corresponding Peter--Weyl decompositions and Sobolev spaces via irreducible representations and the Laplace--Beltrami operator. Combining spectral truncation with finite-depth quantum-circuit approximation, invoking the Solovay--Kitaev theorem, we establish quantitative rates that separate the spectral truncation error from the circuit approximation error.

papers.title: PySymmetry: A Sage/Python Framework for the Symmetry Reduction of Linear G-Equivariant Systems
papers.abstract: Despite the prevalence of symmetry in scientific linear systems, these structural properties are often underutilized by standard computational software. This paper introduces PySymmetry, an open-source Sage/Python framework that implements classical representation theory to simplify G-equivariant linear systems. PySymmetry uses projection operators to generate symmetry-adapted bases, transforming equivariant operators into a more efficient block-diagonal form. Its functionalities include defining and reducing representations, calculating multiplicities, and obtaining the explicit block structure. We demonstrate PySymmetry's versatility through three case studies: a chemistry application, a numerical benchmark on the non-Hermitian Schr\"odinger equation that achieved a performance increase of over 17x compared to standard methods, and a symbolic investigation that enabled the first complete analytical classification of a challenging problem in celestial mechanics. Designed for seamless integration with libraries like NumPy and SciPy, PySymmetry offers a powerful, user-friendly tool for exploring symmetries in theoretical and applied contexts. ```

papers.title: Hook algebras and determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: In characteristic zero, we prove that the Tor algebras of the generic, symmetric, and skew-symmetric determinantal rings are Koszul with respect to a natural regrading. In particular, their Eilenberg--Moore spectral sequence degenerates, which allows us to explicitly determine the Poincar\'e series of their residue fields and answers a problem raised by Avramov. To do this, we construct the universal hook algebra and prove that it has a quadratic Gr\"obner basis and thus is Koszul. This leads to a new standard monomial construction of the irreducible polynomial GL-representations, alongside the Schur and Weyl functors, which is of independent interest.

papers.title: Generating Sets for the Kernels of Frobenius Polarization Operators
papers.abstract: We study generating sets for the kernels of the Frobenius polarization operators associated with elements of finite groups. By applying the discrete Fourier transform on each coset, we describe these kernels in terms of additive semigroups defined by zero-sum relations among roots of unity. We show that the monomials corresponding to the minimal nonzero elements of these semigroups form generating sets of minimum cardinality. We further describe the minimal nonzero elements in the general case in terms of those in the cyclic case and obtain a formula for the minimum number of generators. For the operator associated with a generator of a cyclic group, we also show, as a consequence of known results on integer zero-sum relations and circulant determinant representations, that its kernel and the subalgebra generated by these circulant determinants have the same field of fractions.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil III: Geometric local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the third in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we make the reduction from global arithmetic intersection numbers for special cycles to the local geometric quantities in our companion papers. Building on our previous companion papers, we also propose a construction for arithmetic special cycle classes associated to possibly singular matrices of arbitrary co-rank.

papers.title: Co-rank $1$ Arithmetic Siegel--Weil IV: Analytic local-to-global
papers.abstract: This is the fourth in a sequence of four papers, where we prove the arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula in co-rank $1$ for Kudla--Rapoport special cycles on exotic smooth integral models of unitary Shimura varieties of arbitrarily large even arithmetic dimension. Our arithmetic Siegel--Weil formula implies that degrees of Kudla--Rapoport arithmetic special $1$-cycles are encoded in the first derivatives of unitary Eisenstein series Fourier coefficients. In this paper, we pin down precise normalizations for some $U(m,m)$ Siegel Eisenstein series, give local Siegel--Weil special value formulas with explicit constants, and record a geometric Siegel--Weil result for degrees of complex $0$-cycles. Using this, we complete the proof of our arithmetic Siegel--Weil results by patching together the local main theorems from our companion papers.

papers.title: Matrix Kloosterman sums and product-trace estimates for semisimple algebras
papers.abstract: Let $k=\mathbb{F}_q$, $E=\mathbb{F}_{q^n}$ and $\mathrm{Tr}=\mathrm{Tr}_{E/k}$. For $r\ge 2$, $a\in k^{\times}$ and $x\in E^{\times}$, let $\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)$ be the number of $r$-tuples $(x_1,\cdots,x_r)$ in $(E^{\times})^r$ satisfying $x_1\cdots x_r=x$ and $\mathrm{Tr}(x_1+\cdots+x_r)=a$. We prove $\left|\mathrm{N}(E,r,x,a)-\left((q^n-1)^{r-1}+(-1)^r\right)/q\right|\le (r^n-1) q^{\frac{(r-1)n-1}{2}}$. This proves the square-root estimate predicted in Wan's conjecture and generalizes a previous result of Moisio and Wan. For a finite semisimple algebra $B=\prod\limits_{i=1}^s M_{d_i}(\mathbb{F}_{q^{n_i}})$ over $k$ and a regular element $x\in B^{\times}$, the same method combined with Zelingher's formula leads to analogous square-root estimates.

papers.title: Gorenstein cotorsion pairs induced by balanced pairs
papers.abstract: Let $(\mathcal{X},\mathcal{Y})$ be an admissible balanced pair in a locally presentable abelian category $\mathcal{A}$, and let $\mathcal{E}$ be its induced exact structure. We study the class $G(\mathcal{X})$ of cycles of two-sided complexes with terms in $\mathcal{X}$ that are both right and left $\mathcal{X}$-acyclic. If $\mathcal{X}$ is closed under direct summands and finite direct sums and is $\kappa$-Kaplansky for every sufficiently large regular cardinal $\kappa$, we prove that $(G(\mathcal{X}),G(\mathcal{X})^{\perp *})$ is a hereditary cotorsion pair relative to $\mathcal E$. For relative purity determined by finitely presented modules, we give two criteria for functorial completeness and show that relative periodic modules generate a functorially complete hereditary cotorsion pair. We also compute the relative Gorenstein objects, their right orthogonal, and explicit approximations for a family of exact structures over Dedekind domains.

papers.title: Equivariant Steklov homogenisation and stability of spectral representations
papers.abstract: We prove that isolated spectral clusters preserve their finite-group representation under equivariant spectral convergence. In particular, an irreducible limiting eigenspace cannot split into several nearby eigenvalues, while an isotypic limiting eigenspace imposes corresponding divisibility constraints on the multiplicities in the approximating cluster. We then construct a one-parameter equivariant Steklov homogenisation on closed orientable surfaces, allowing Laplace spectral representations to be transferred to Steklov spectral clusters. Applied to the hyperbolic surfaces of Fortier Bourque, Gruda-Mediavilla, Petri, and Pineault, this yields first Steklov multiplicities 16 and 21 in genera 10 and 17, and at least 24 in genus 37. These examples give counterexamples to Jammes's conjecture on first Steklov multiplicity.

papers.title: Actions of Fell bundles, II: tensor products and Fourier-Stieltjes algebras
papers.abstract: In the context of Fell bundles over discrete groups, we introduce and analyze suitable notions of direct sum and tensor product of actions of Fell bundles on Hilbert bundles. For $C^*$-dynamical systems, where actions arise from equivariant representations, we discuss how the tensor product of two such actions is related to the action associated with the tensor product of the underlying equivariant representations. Likewise, since any action gives rise to a $C^*$-correspondence between the full cross-sectional $C^*$-algebras of the involved Fell bundles, we examine the connection between the $C^*$-correspondence associated with the tensor product of two given actions and the tensor product of the associated $C^*$-correspondences. We also discuss how the tensor product of actions naturally appears in Rieffel-like induction processes. Finally we present related results on the Fourier-Stieltjes and Fourier algebras of a Fell bundle.

papers.title: On the saturability of $p$-adic Lie groups
papers.abstract: Lazard theory is becoming increasingly important in $p$-adic representation theory, especially when studying mod $p$ representations. For $G$ a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $K/\mathbb Q_p$, a question going back to Lazard is when a pro-$p$ Iwahori subgroup of $G(K)$ admits a saturated $p$-valuation. In this article, we establish a deep connection to Moy-Prasad theory, and show that the Moy-Prasad filtration defines a saturated $p$-valuation on $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$ for any point $x$ in the semisimple Bruhat-Tits building of $G$, given a mild assumption on the maximal torus of $G$ and that $p>2$. We also compute Lazard Lie algebras defined over $\mathbb Z_p$ and the polynomial ring $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$ associated to the saturated group $G_{x,\frac{1}{p-1}+}$, which allows us to reinterpret the Moy-Prasad isomorphism as an isomorphism of Lie algebras over $\mathbb F_p[\varepsilon]$.

papers.title: Higher mod $p$ Satake transforms: explicit formulas and images for $\mathrm{GL}_2$
papers.abstract: Heyer's left adjoint to derived parabolic induction gives rise to higher mod $p$ Satake transforms \[ \mathcal S_V^i: \mathcal H_G(V) \longrightarrow \mathcal H_M\bigl(H^i(K_U,V)\bigr), \] whose extreme degrees recover Herzig's invariant and coinvariant transforms. For $G=\mathbf G(F)$, where $\mathbf G$ is a connected reductive group defined over a finite extension $F/\mathbb{Q}_p$, we describe these maps explicitly using Mackey decompositions and corestriction in group cohomology. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, we evaluate them on the standard Hecke generators, showing that their support lies in a single Weyl orbit and that their values on the individual support cosets are concrete corestriction operators. For $G=\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$, we determine the image in every cohomological degree for each non-Steinberg Serre weight. The endpoint images are the classical polynomial Satake images, while every interior image is of the form \[ k[x,y^{\pm1}]/(x^r) \] for some positive integer $r$. Thus, every interior image is a finite nilpotent thickening of the Laurent polynomial algebra $k[y^{\pm1}]$. We give explicit bounds for its thickness, prove that they are sharp, and show that in the unramified case every interior image is either reduced or a square-zero thickening.

papers.title: Lusztig Parameters and Factorizations of Determinantial Modules
papers.abstract: We give an explicit formula for the Lusztig parameters of determinantial modules over symmetric quiver Hecke algebras. The formula applies to every Bruhat pair and every fixed reduced expression of the upper Weyl group element. In finite types $A$, $D$, and $E$, we identify the parameters of the modules in M\'enard's seed using Demazure weaves. We then factor prefix determinantial modules into these seed modules, with multiplicities given by Lusztig cycles. We also give a criterion for recognizing monomials in this fixed seed and an explicit formula recovering their multiplicities from Lusztig parameters.

papers.title: Global obstruction property and its applications
papers.abstract: We introduce the global obstruction property (GOP) for Artin algebras: for every finitely generated module of infinite projective dimension, two distinct syzygies have a common nonprojective indecomposable direct summand. We prove that GOP implies the generalized Auslander--Reiten condition, and hence the Auslander--Reiten conjecture. We give criteria for GOP to hold for pullbacks over semisimple algebras and construct an example which is not syzygy-finite. For each Artin algebra $A$, we construct an algebra $\mathcal{G}(A)$ satisfying GOP by using triangular matrix extensions. We show that $\text{fin.dim}\mathcal{G}(A)=\text{fin.dim} A+2$ and that $A$ and $\mathcal{G}(A)$ are singularly equivalent. Finally, we give a pair of derived equivalent finite-dimensional algebras for which GOP holds on only one side.

papers.title: Haar measure for totally positive split real semisimple quantum groups of classical type
papers.abstract: Let $\hbar$ be a non-zero real number and put $q= e^{-\pi i \hbar}$. Let $G$ be a semisimple split real Lie group of classical type, with Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ and associated Borel subalgebra $\mathfrak{b} \subseteq \mathfrak{g}$. We show that there exists a locally compact quantum group $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$ which integrates the Borel part $U_q(\mathfrak{b})$ of the Drinfeld--Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra $U_q(\mathfrak{g})$, viewed as a Hopf $*$-algebra. We further compute the associated Haar weights and modular data for $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$. Up to an excess Cartan part, the Drinfeld double of $(L_{\hbar}(B),\Delta)$ can be seen as an analytic quantization of the function algebra of the totally positive semigroup $G^+\subseteq G$.

papers.title: A 9-dimensional nilpotent Lie algebra isomorphic to its complex conjugate admitting no real form
papers.abstract: We give an explicit example of a 9-dimensional 5-step nilpotent complex Lie algebra, generated by two elements, that is isomorphic to its complex conjugate but has no real form. In contrast to the earlier 10-dimensional examples, our proof is completely elementary and very short.

papers.title: Motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells and the connective formal group law
papers.abstract: We use the connective formal group law to define a one-parameter ($\beta$-)deformation of the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells in the $d$-step flag variety. This $\beta$-deformation specializes to the motivic Segre classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=1$ and to the Segre-Schwartz-MacPherson classes of Schubert cells when $\beta=0$ (though the $\beta$-deformations are not simply the $\beta$-homogenizations of the motivic Segre classes). We define rational function representatives for the $\beta$-deformed classes in the $d=1$ case in terms of a solvable lattice model, and we prove a combinatorial formula for the structure constants in the $\beta$-deformed basis in the $d=1$ case using Knutson-Tao puzzles. Unexpectedly, the structure constants are built out of entries of $R$-matrices for the multi-parameter quantum group of type $\widehat{a}_2$ (which suggests an action of multi-parameter quantum groups on equivariant connective $K$-rings of Nakajima quiver varieties, with their convolution algebra structures). We show that our $\beta$-deformations arise from canonical elements in a quotient of the torus-equivariant algebraic cobordism ring of the cotangent bundle of the flag variety by proving that the canonical elements satisfy a GKM type condition (in future work, we will show that these canonical elements also lie in the torus-equivariant connective $K$-ring, in the sense of Karpenko--Merkurjev, of this cotangent bundle).

papers.title: On (super)symmetrizing forms and Schur elements of cyclotomic Hecke-Clifford algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper, we introduce Schur elements for supersymmetrizing superalgebras. We show that the cyclotomic Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}^f_{c}(n)$ is supersymmetric if $f=f^{(\mathtt{0})}_{\underline{Q}}$ and, symmetric if $f=f^{(\mathtt{s})}_{\underline{Q}}$ and an invertibility condition holds. In the semisimple case, we compute the Schur elements for both $\mathcal{H}^f_{c}(n)$ and the cyclotomic Sergeev algebra $\mathcal{h}^g_{c}(n)$. As applications, we define new symmetrizing forms on the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}(n)$ and on the cyclotomic quiver Hecke algebras of types $A^{(1)}_{e-1}$ and $C^{(1)}_e$.

papers.title: Bicompact torsion classes and conjectures on brick infinite algebras
papers.abstract: In the category $\operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ of finitely generated modules over a finite dimensional algebra $A$, a torsion class $\mathcal{T} \subset \operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ is said to be compact if there exists a module $M \in \operatorname{\mathsf{mod}} A$ such that $\mathcal{T}$ is the smallest torsion class containing $M$. If a torsion class satisfies this and the dual condition, then we call it a bicompact torsion class. We conjecture that bicompact torsion classes are precisely functorially finite torsion classes, and prove it for hereditary algebras and also for semistable torsion classes. This gives that Demonet's Lattice Point Conjecture implies Enomoto's Infinite Semibrick Conjecture, both of which are important conjectures on brick infiniteness.

papers.title: Right representations of Novikov algebras
papers.abstract: We study the theory of right representations of Novikov algebras. We introduce the notion of a modular right ideal of a Novikov algebra and prove that every irreducible right representation of a Novikov algebra is isomorphic to the quotient by a maximal modular right ideal. We prove that the class of Novikov algebras with no irreducible representations forms a hereditary radical. We introduce the notion of a primitive Novikov algebra and show that a Novikov algebra is primitive if and only if it admits an almost faithful irreducible representation. We also introduce the notion of the quasi-kernel of a representation, defined as the largest ideal contained in its kernel. Finally, we prove that the constructed radical coincides with the intersection of the quasi-kernels of all its irreducible representations.

papers.title: Regularity and the Gelfand Property for Complex Symmetric Pairs
papers.abstract: We prove that every symmetric pair of a connected complex reductive group is regular in the sense of Aizenbud--Gourevitch. This settles the Aizenbud--Gourevitch regularity conjecture over the complex numbers. Generalized Harish--Chandra descent then makes the canonical central cover of every complex symmetric pair a Gelfand--Kazhdan pair. An anti-automorphism arising from a compatible Chevalley involution upgrades the resulting GP2 bound to GP1 on the cover, and finite central descent transfers GP1 to the original pair. In particular, van Dijk's conjecture on complex symmetric pairs follows. Rubio reduced the unresolved irreducible regularity problem to four families: the DIII family $(D_r,A_{r-1}+\mathbb{C})$, the balanced CII family $(C_{2r},C_r+C_r)$, some remaining Spin block pairs, and the EVII pair $(E_7,E_6+\mathbb{C})$. We treat these cases by four different mechanisms. For DIII we construct a sign-equivariant Schwartz distribution on the regular set and extend it across a common orbit boundary by the Chen--Sun theorem. For balanced CII we combine homogeneity, distinguished nilpotent orbits, and a stable-density theorem for the centralizer representation. For Spin blocks we prove pleasantness for unequal odd--odd blocks, use Przebinda's orthogonal-distribution theorem in odd smaller rank, and construct a finite orbit closure with automatic extension in even smaller rank. For EVII we compute the graded-$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ data for all twenty-two nilpotent orbits and use central-torus characters to eliminate the remaining resonances, including the two residual triple-centralizer cases. A finite-component assembly theorem then handles arbitrary connected central quotients and diagonal couplings among simple factors.
